waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk River Trailhead
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass required at the kiosk; this has been the primary approach since the White Chuck River Trail washed out in 2003.
waypoints.directions: The North Fork Sauk River Trailhead sits at about 2,050 ft off FR 49, the Sloan Creek Road, and it is where Trail #649 starts up the valley. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and there is a kiosk at the trailhead. Do not plan on coming in from the west: the White Chuck River Road (FR 23) remains washed out, and this has been the primary approach to Glacier Peak since the White Chuck River Trail washed out in 2003.

waypoints.name: Mackinaw Shelter (former shelter site)
waypoints.note: Old-growth riverside camp; the actual shelter is gone/unsafe, use the established sites nearby, last reliable flat camping before the climb steepens.
waypoints.directions: Follow the North Fork Sauk trail up-valley on a mellow, rolling, well-maintained grade through old-growth forest, with a few scattered campsites along the way. The old shelter site is the last of the low-elevation river camps; past it the trail leaves the valley floor and steepens sharply.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk Trail / PCT junction near White Pass
waypoints.note: Trail gains ~3,000 ft in the final stretch to this meadow junction with sweeping views of Glacier Peak; join the PCT here.
waypoints.directions: Beyond the old shelter site the trail turns into roughly three miles of switchbacks, gaining about 3,000 ft to the meadows at White Pass. Water is unreliable once you leave the river, so fill up before starting the climb. The PCT junction is at the top.

waypoints.name: Glacier Gap
waypoints.note: Large, popular camp area with many established sites on a broad gap; standard base camp for the Gerdine Ridge/Cool Glacier route.
waypoints.directions: Continue northeast across the basin, gaining a few hundred feet to the broad gap where the White Chuck and Suiattle glaciers meet. Established sites are spread across the gap, and it is the last flat ground before the summit push.

waypoints.name: Cool Glacier saddle (Gerdine-Cool col)
waypoints.note: Saddle between Disappointment Peak and Glacier Peak where the Gerdine Ridge route tops out onto the Cool Glacier for the final push.
waypoints.directions: Leave camp on crampons, losing a little height onto rocky Gerdine Ridge, then climb north, contouring the slope below Glacier Gap Peak before regaining the crest and following it to roughly 8,400 ft. The climber's track ends near a gendarme around 8,500 ft — rope up there, traverse northeast onto the Gerdine and upper Suiattle ice, and end-run one or two crevasses where it bends into the Cool Glacier. Keep moving on that traverse; the cliffs of Disappointment Peak above it shed rock. Finish by climbing west up the Cool Glacier to regain the ridge at the saddle.

waypoints.name: Glacier Peak summit
waypoints.note: True summit of Glacier Peak (Dakobed); broad volcanic summit with views across the North Cascades.
waypoints.directions: From the saddle the glacier travel is over. Rejoin the climber's trail and finish up one short, steep pitch of pumice and broken volcanic rock to the top — unroped class 2-3, with no rock gear needed.

sources: USGS GNIS DomesticNames_WA (1519988 Glacier Peak, 1518794 Disappointment Peak, 1528075 White Pass)

waypoints.name: Mt. Pugh Trailhead #644
waypoints.note: Mountain Loop Highway to FR-2095. Trail passes Lake Metan (1.5 mi) en route to Stujack Pass.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 exit 208, drive east on SR-530 through Arlington to Darrington, about 28 miles, then turn right at the four-way stop in town onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow it south roughly 14 miles — paved at first, then graveled — to FR-2095, the Mt. Pugh Spur Road, marked with a large sign on the left. Turn onto FR-2095, a narrow, one-lane, unpaved road, and continue about 1.5 miles to the trailhead on the right; the trailhead lot itself holds only a handful of cars, so use the large pullout at the switchback just below it if it's full. FR-2095 is gated from October 16 to June 1 for wildlife, on top of whatever winter closure may be in effect on the Mountain Loop Highway itself.

waypoints.name: Lake Metan
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail #644 about 1.5 miles through old-growth forest, with several stream crossings and about 1,300 ft of gain, to Lake Metan. It is the last reliable water on the route.

waypoints.name: Stujack Pass
waypoints.directions: Round the north side of the lake and switchback steeply up through forest, then talus and meadows past an open boulder basin near 4,900 ft, to the notch of Stujack Pass at about 5,700 ft, where the maintained trail ends. Snow often lingers on this stretch into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Mount Pugh Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb left out of the notch on heather, contour the east side of the ridge and cross the head of a small permanent snowfield, then follow the knife-edge crest on chipped, blasted ledges past the short Class 3 chimney with an iron ring. Ignore stray cairns that lead toward the cliff edge. The true high point is a roughly 10 ft boulder at the edge of the flat summit plateau.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to Forest Road 2095 (FR-2095)
road.status: Closed now: the Forest Service keeps FR 2095 gated at the Mountain Loop Highway each year from 16 October to 1 June, for wildlife.
road.driveNote: From the Darrington Ranger District office, follow the Mountain Loop Highway about 14 miles, then turn left (east) onto signed FR 2095 and go roughly 1 mile to the trailhead on the right. Parking is very limited; the large pullout at the switchback below takes the overflow.
road.seasonalGate: Gated every year from 16 October to 1 June. Darrington Ranger District: (360) 436-1155.

waypoints.name: Tucquala Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.note: FS 4330 (Cle Elum Valley Rd), about 11 mi past Salmon La Sac. Standard access for Peggys Pond via Cathedral Pass Trail #1345 to Cathedral Pass, continuing to Mount Daniel's SE slopes/Daniel Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Drive up the Cle Elum River valley on Forest Service Road 4330 (Cle Elum Valley Road), about 11 miles past Salmon La Sac, to its end at the trailhead, 3,370 feet. The access road is rough gravel and is best driven with a high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle.

waypoints.name: Peggys Pond
waypoints.directions: Take the Cathedral Rock Trail #1345, which crosses the Cle Elum River on a bridge and climbs past Squaw Lake to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail, about 4.5 miles. Follow the PCT briefly toward Deep Lake; at the first switchback down, take the spur to Peggys Pond, about half a mile of steep, narrow path along ledges with sheer drop-offs and loose rock.

waypoints.name: Mount Daniel (true/West Summit)
waypoints.directions: Follow braided boot paths northwest then west across heather and talus, gaining about 1,500 ft in a mile to the broad southeast ridge near 7,000 ft, with the Hyas Creek Glacier on your right and Circle Lake below on your left. Traverse climbers' trail and scree below the East Summit to the 7,600-ft saddle, then cross loose talus, snow and the rocky glacier margin to the West Summit, staying on rock off the glacier ice.

sources: USGS GNIS DomesticNames_WA (1524305 Peggys Pond, 1518479 Mount Daniel)
